item.title: Squeak 2.34.8
item.description:
One roster everywhere, a calmer top, and ducklings in tabs.

  • Every place that shows a pond's ducks (the Dashboard numbers, the duck list, tabs, the subheader, For you, the sidebar) now reads one list from your Mac, so counts, status and streams always agree. A duck whose ducklings are still working shows as working.
  • The top bar and a duck's subheader sit on one quiet surface: borderless tabs, a frosted Dashboard | Room switch, and a soft hint of the pond's colour that fades out quickly. Bright pond colours stay muted everywhere.
  • Opening a duckling opens it as a tab next to its duck. Esc or ⌘W takes you back.

Also in 2.34.7

Fixes and polish for the new layout.

  • Choosing Room in the top bar now always shows the Room, coming back from a duck too.
  • The top bar has proper spacing; the Dashboard | Room switch and the tabs share one height, and tabs size to what they say.
  • Inside a duck, the pond's colour runs as one smooth gradient from under the bar into the chat.
  • Message actions (time, Copy, more) sit under each reply instead of over the text. In the Room, Reply, Copy and Make task appear in the gap under a message.
  • In the Room, a note from one duck to another reads as one line with an @mention, with the full message one click away. Old duck names no longer show numbers.
  • Your Room messages show your initials; task cards follow the message column.
  • Skip approvals never asks again, also for ducks working in the pond's main folder.
  • Unread marks only follow finished turns, not Squeak's own housekeeping notes.

Also in 2.34.6

One bar with tabs, a calmer Room, and ducks that choose their own streams.

  • One bar on every page: the pond's logo and name, the Dashboard | Room switch, then tabs. Each duck is a low oval tab showing what its chat is for and what it's doing right now; files, diffs and artifacts open as tabs beside them. Inside a duck the bar stays put, with the duck's streams, commit and PR controls just below it.
  • The Room reads like a group chat: whole messages in flat rows, each task as one card that updates in place, and an unread line. Tap a message or a duck to open its chat at that moment. Ducks write short Room updates themselves; status chatter stays in their own chats.
  • Ducks start in the pond and open, join or leave streams themselves, even two at once. Their streams show under the bar and in Changes. Main stays read-only for ducks.
  • Duck names are short, many with an Indian touch, and never have a number. A duck gives its name back when it goes off duty; off-duty ducks are listed by what their chat was for. Chats get clear titles once their work is clear.
  • The Files, Changes, Artifacts and Tasks lists on the right open at once.
  • If a duck's stream folder is gone, its chat says so and offers Return to the Pond, instead of a confusing error.
  • Fewer buttons: every control has a reason to be there.
